//: Dev-only. `ng serve` on :4200 forwards these prefixes to the Flask admin
on :1234, so the browser sees one origin and the SPA's relative URLs work
unchanged between `ng serve` and the container.
Same-origin is not cosmetic here: the API authenticates by session cookie,
and EventSource cannot send headers. A cross-origin dev setup would need
CORS plus SameSite=None, i.e. a development environment exercising a
different auth path from production -- which is where a whole class of
/static is proxied as well as /api because the SPA loads both vendored
fonts from Flask (see src/styles/fonts.css) rather than bundling them.
Without it, `ng serve` renders in the fallback system font and nobody
notices until a screenshot looks wrong.
This file is NEVER referenced from docker-compose.yml. The container
serves the built bundle from Flask; there is no ng serve in production,
and a proxy config that leaked into the image would be a second, silent
Start it with: npm start  (see angular.json's serve.options.proxyConfig)
